identity.real_world_identity_notes: Third-generation Chevrolet Corvette. Its four-speed manual came in wide-ratio M20, close-ratio M21 and heavy-duty close-ratio M22 forms, standard from 1970 and available through 1981.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift and blips to downshift.
The source names three four-speed variants and the drive cannot distinguish them, so no specific gearbox is claimed beyond the four-speed manual itself.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.
This class reports a single configuration; the selection screen offers no aero package and only the plain identity has been observed.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.chevrolet-corvette-c3.20260815t233851406z-a0ef2751 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by a registered source.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the C3 Corvette and its four-speed manual, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source gives a four-speed manual in three ratio sets, and the live drive selected four H-pattern gears. The source does not say which of the three AMS2 models.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim. The clutch for a shift already under way follows from gearbox construction, not from the drive.

Derived from the established synchromesh construction: a synchromesh gearbox is shifted with the clutch as authentic technique, and a clutchless shift is a trick the simulator allows rather than how the car was driven.

driver_summary: The C3's four-speed came in wide-ratio M20, close-ratio M21 and heavy-duty M22 forms, and no source says which AMS2 models. Synchronised either way, so the blip eases the synchros but the gear engages without it.
